title: Extension of all basis identifications at a continuous ordinal limit
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal B$ be a set of open subsets covering $X$, with $U\cap V=\bigcup_{T\in\mathcal B,\,T\subset U\cap V}T$ for $U,V\in\mathcal B$. For every $U\in\mathcal B$ give $K_U\in D(\mathcal O_U)$ [def-pc-derived-category] and for every inclusion $V\subset U$ in $\mathcal B$ give an isomorphism $\rho_V^U:K_U|_V\xrightarrow{\sim}K_V$, with $\rho_U^U=1$ and $\rho_T^U=\rho_T^V\circ(\rho_V^U|_T)$ for $T\subset V\subset U$. Assume $\operatorname{Hom}(K_U,K_U[i])=0$ for every $U\in\mathcal B$ and every integer $i<0$. For a union $O$ of members of $\mathcal B$, put $\mathcal B_O=\{U\in\mathcal B:U\subset O\}$. A solution on $O$ means an object $F\in D(\mathcal O_O)$ with isomorphisms $s_U:F|_U\xrightarrow{\sim}K_U$ for every $U\in\mathcal B_O$, satisfying $\rho_V^U\circ(s_U|_V)=s_V$ for all inclusions $V\subset U$ in $\mathcal B_O$. Let $\lambda$ be a nonzero set-sized limit ordinal and let $(W_\beta)_{\beta<\lambda}$ be increasing unions of members of $\mathcal B$, with $W_0=\varnothing$ and $W_\delta=\bigcup_{\beta<\delta}W_\beta$ for every nonzero limit $\delta<\lambda$. Put $W_\lambda=\bigcup_{\beta<\lambda}W_\beta$. Suppose solutions $(F_\beta,s_\beta)$ on $W_\beta$ are supplied, with $\operatorname{Hom}(F_\beta,F_\beta[i])=0$ for $i<0$, and isomorphisms $r_\gamma^\beta:F_\beta|_{W_\gamma}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_\gamma$ for $\gamma<\beta<\lambda$. Assume $r_\eta^\beta=r_\eta^\gamma\circ(r_\gamma^\beta|_{W_\eta})$ for $\eta<\gamma<\beta$ and $s_{\gamma,U}\circ(r_\gamma^\beta|_U)=s_{\beta,U}$ for $U\in\mathcal B_{W_\gamma}$. Then there are a solution $(F_\lambda,s_\lambda)$ on $W_\lambda$ and isomorphisms $r_\beta:F_\lambda|_{W_\beta}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_\beta$ with $r_\gamma^\beta\circ(r_\beta|_{W_\gamma})=r_\gamma$ and $s_{\lambda,U}=s_{\beta,U}\circ(r_\beta|_U)$ for every $U\in\mathcal B_{W_\beta}$. For each $U\in\mathcal B_{W_\lambda}$, the map $s_{\lambda,U}$ is the unique morphism $F_\lambda|_U\to K_U$ satisfying $\rho_V^U\circ(s_{\lambda,U}|_V)=s_{\beta,V}\circ(r_\beta|_V)$ for all $\beta<\lambda$ and $V\in\mathcal B$ with $V\subset U\cap W_\beta$; it is an isomorphism. No member $U\in\mathcal B_{W_\lambda}$ is required to lie in a single $W_\beta$, and no quasi-compactness or boundedness is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0D6B (cohomology-lemma-glueing-increasing-union) and 0D6C (cohomology-theorem-glueing-bbd-general), limit step and final compatibility bookkeeping.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-derived-basis-increasing-union] on the open subscheme $W_\lambda$, with $K_\beta=F_\beta$. The ordinal is set-sized, the opens cover $W_\lambda$, continuity includes $W_0=\varnothing$, and the required negative self Hom and cocycle are hypotheses. Obtain $F_\lambda$ and $r_\beta:F_\lambda|_{W_\beta}\cong F_\beta$ with $r_\gamma=r_\gamma^\beta\circ(r_\beta|_{W_\gamma})$.

Fix $U\in\mathcal B_{W_\lambda}$ and put $\mathcal C_U=\{V\in\mathcal B:V\subset U\cap W_\beta\text{ for some }\beta<\lambda\}$. It covers $U$: for $x\in U$, choose a stage containing $x$, a member $T\in\mathcal B$ containing $x$ inside that stage, and then a member $V$ containing $x$ inside $T\cap U$. Intersections of two members are covered by members of $\mathcal C_U$, using the original intersection property and the fact that any smaller member remains in the same stage. For $V\subset U\cap W_\beta$ define $a_V=(\rho_V^U)^{-1}\circ s_{\beta,V}\circ(r_\beta|_V)$. If $\beta\le\gamma$ are two choices, the equations $r_\beta=r_\beta^\gamma(r_\gamma|_{W_\beta})$ and $s_{\beta,V}(r_\beta^\gamma|_V)=s_{\gamma,V}$ show the two formulas agree (equality of indices is immediate). Thus $a_V$ is well defined. For $T\subset V$ in $\mathcal C_U$, choose a stage for $V$, hence also for $T$; the cocycle for $\rho$ and the solution equation for $s_\beta$ give $a_V|_T=a_T$.

source.place: Tag 0D6C (cohomology-theorem-glueing-bbd-general), final paragraph: the system on U

proof.text: On each $V\in\mathcal C_U$, both $F_\lambda|_V$ and $K_U|_V$ are isomorphic to $K_V$, via $s_{\beta,V}(r_\beta|_V)$ and $\rho_V^U$. Consequently the negative Hom hypotheses hold for both ordered cross pairs and both self pairs, by conjugating with these isomorphisms and their shifts. Apply [lem-trf-derived-basis-local-hom-glue] on the scheme $U$, with covering collection $\mathcal C_U$, to glue the $a_V$ to a unique morphism $s_{\lambda,U}:F_\lambda|_U\to K_U$. Apply it to the inclusion-compatible inverse family $a_V^{-1}$ to obtain $b_U$. For the two self pairs, Hom injectivity identifies $b_Us_{\lambda,U}$ and $s_{\lambda,U}b_U$ with the identities, since they restrict to identities on every $V$. Thus $s_{\lambda,U}$ is an isomorphism. Its restriction equation is precisely $\rho_V^U(s_{\lambda,U}|_V)=s_{\beta,V}(r_\beta|_V)$. Hom injectivity also proves uniqueness among all morphisms satisfying these equations.

source.place: Tags 0D68 (cohomology-lemma-uniqueness) and 0D6C, final paragraph: existence and uniqueness on U

proof.text: For $T\subset U$ in $\mathcal B_{W_\lambda}$ compare $\rho_T^U(s_{\lambda,U}|_T)$ with $s_{\lambda,T}$. On every $V\in\mathcal C_T$, contained in some $W_\beta$, the restriction of the first is $\rho_T^U|_V(\rho_V^U)^{-1}s_{\beta,V}(r_\beta|_V)=(\rho_V^T)^{-1}s_{\beta,V}(r_\beta|_V)$ by the original cocycle. This is the restriction of the second by Step 3. Apply Hom injectivity in [lem-trf-derived-basis-local-hom-glue] on $T$ for $F_\lambda|_T,K_T$ and the cover $\mathcal C_T$; its local negative Hom follows from their identifications with $K_V$. The two maps are equal. Hence the maps just constructed form a solution on every member, including those crossing all earlier stages.

source.place: Tag 0D6C, last sentence: explicit inclusion-compatibility bookkeeping

proof.text: If $U\in\mathcal B_{W_\beta}$, then $U$ itself belongs to $\mathcal C_U$. The defining equation at $V=U$ and $\rho_U^U=1$ give $s_{\lambda,U}=s_{\beta,U}(r_\beta|_U)$. Together with Step 1 this gives all stage comparisons. If $U=\varnothing$ or $W_\lambda=\varnothing$, the same Hom bijections apply: [lem-trf-derived-basis-local-hom-glue] explicitly includes the empty scheme and empty covering family. The argument uses only set-sized covers; no finite subcover, boundedness, or containment of $U$ in one stage was used.
